description.narrative:
Originally, the project expected to work with five outcomes which would contribute to increased resilience and womens and girls empowerment.
1. Service providers (both public and local government institutions) are responsive, and increased access to the quality services of community, especially women and girls.
2. Improved resilience of the most vulnerable coastal, char, hill, and haor communities to climate change impact.
3. Empowered women and girls are dealing with inequality, social injustice, violence incidences and participate in voice raising and protests.
4. Strong voices and decisions are in place against violence against women and child marriage. Decrease in rate of child marriage and violence against women in the selected climate vulnerable areas.
5. Risks related to poverty will be decreased with increased family income and alternative livelihoods options.
In addtion to the above, the project objectives will now also include:
6. Strengthen democratic institutions, promote transparency and accountability, support civic engagement, and advocate for human rights.
7. Empower youth and women through leadership development, civic education, and skills training; promote gender equality; address gender-based violence; and ensure inclusive decision-making for all.
8. Prevent harassment and promote civility on public transportation by raising awareness and encouraging positive behavior through visually impactful messages displayed in the Dhaka metro and buses.

Projektet syftar till att bygga samhällens motståndskraft, särskilt kvinnors och flickor, mot de sociala effekterna av klimatförändringar såsom könsbaserat våld och barnäktenskap. Genom implementering av de planerade aktiviteterna under 2022 till och med 2026 kommer projektet att höja kapaciteten för både rättighetsinnehavare och pliktbärare så att rättighetsinnehavare kan dra nytta av klimatanpassad försörjning och pliktbärare kan svara effektivt på människors krav.
Genusdimensionen är ett av de viktigaste områdena som omfattas av insatsen. Kritiska områden att ta itu med är klimatfattigdom, reproduktiv hälsa, barns utbildning och könsbaserat våld.

The project aims to build communities' resilience, especially that of women and girls, against the social impacts of climate change such as gender-based violence and child marriage. Through implementation of the planned activities during 2022 through 2026, the project will enhance the capacity of both rights holders and duty bearers so that rights holders can benefit from climate-adaptive livelihood and duty bearers can respond effectively to people's demands.
The gender dimension is one of the major areas to be covered by the intervention. Critical areas to be addressed include climate poverty, reproductive health, children’s education, and gender-based violence.

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

description.narrative:
This period (September 2023 - August 2024) was marked by both progress and massive socio-political shifts, most notably the July revolution a turning point that underscored the urgency for civic engagement, accountable governance, and inclusive development. While the political upheaval created temporary disruptions in some project areas, it also ignited a renewed sense of agency at the grassroots level. Community leaders, particularly women and youth, expressed a stronger desire to organize, speak out, and influence local decision-making. In several districts, MJF partners reported increased engagement from citizens who had previously felt excluded from governance processes.
Progress and Results:
Outcome 1 (institutional Delivery): Collaboration with local service providers and government institutions has been deepened to improve the inclusiveness, accessibility, and responsiveness of public services, particularly for women and girls in climate-vulnerable areas. An example is that participatory planning processes including a greater percentage of women resulted in localized action plans that are now guiding improvements in service delivery.
Outcome 2 (Improved Resilience): The project advanced community-driven climate adaptation with a strong focus on womens leadership and participation. E.g; action plans to enhance climate resilience developed through participatory processes led to community members being benefited (a large percentage of them women).
Outcome 3 (Empowerment of Women and Girls): It has been reported that there has been an improvement legal awareness and protection for women and girls through orientation sessions on legal rights, child marriage, and domestic violence. Several participants reported using this knowledge to intervene in early marriage cases or seek support for domestic abuse. Activities related to policy influence has facilitated the integration of gender perspectives into local climate policies and programming. As a result, several district-level actors committed to incorporating gender-responsive strategies into upcoming climate action plans.
Outcome 4 (Sexual and Gender based Violence): Contribution to changing social norms at the household level. E.g; through activities across diverse cultural settings, the project has fostered open conversations around early marriage, education for girls, and shared caregiving roles.These sessions contributed to more supportive environments for adolescent girls within families.
Outcome 5 (Reduced Poverty): Through their engagement in economic empowerment initiatives, women have been able to access interest-free funds to embark on climate-resilient income-generating activities (IGAs) and participate in cooperative savings schemes. As a result, over 70% of participants reported increased household income and improved capacity to manage climate-induced financial shocks. Strategic livelihood optionssuch as homestead gardening, goat rearing, and tailoring were selected to enhance sustainability, reduce time poverty, and strengthen womens decision-making autonomy. These efforts have not only improved financial stability but also fostered long-term resilience in vulnerable communities.
